title_en: Why Koreans sleep at a spa for about $10 🥚 #shorts
description_en:
In Korea, a 찜질방 (jjimjilbang) is a spa you sleep in. You pay once at the door — about ten dollars — and get pajamas, a towel, hot rooms, cold rooms and a shower. Then everyone sits on the warm floor cracking boiled eggs. Some people crack them on their own foreheads. Then they sleep there, all night, next to strangers.

Stock footage: Pexels (free license)
